title: Chapter 40
text: ∫ 5 cats cat A: old granny, pointed teeth, she’s seen too much, she doesn’t give a damn about the Russian Revolution or any others; Harry Truman playing the piano with Lauren Bacall plopped thereupon doesn’t matter; she’s mean because to survive is sometimes mean. cat B: a bland fellow, gets along with all the other cats and he likes to sleep against my lower leg at night, left leg while I’m on my back, right leg when I’m on my belly and he’s heard Johnny Carson and maybe has seen him but like me he never laughs at that. cat C: the clown, big boy, huge eyes, he’s tan and white, the favorite of the cat hospital, they think he’s funny but when he goes out at night there are soon horrible screams from the darkness. he’s killed one of the neighbors cats, mutilated another. he returns with tufts of fur sticking out of his mouth, endless scratches, dried blood, swellings, ripped tail, ripped paw, he’s had one broken leg, he’s always back at the hospital, he’s so often bandaged, red and white bandages, he rips them off, we jam antibiotic pills into his mouth and try to keep him in at night. he’s never read Schopenhauer but would dig hell out of him. cat D: the mother of cats B and C. and all the cats chase her except B. cat E does too but I haven’t told you about cat E. stick around. anyhow, cat D gets most of the love from us, her existence is so damned, she just hides and hides and licks her grievous wounds. if she could read she would probably wax to the sisters Brontë. cat E: just came to the door one day, all black, the perfect animal, each movement slides through space without friction, he’s the leopard, those yellow eyes look at you and say: kill or be killed, he is centuries old, the other cats stay away from him, including the great fighter: C. it’s the EYES, they can’t handle those EYES. he will never be tamed yet manage to pick him up, stroke him, put him down, he will follow you for some minutes, purring: he is thanking you for not murdering him. he’d scare hell out of Charles Manson and if he had to choose from such things in a milder moment he might possibly go Celine. anyhow, all these strange hunks of life let us know how alone we are forever and yet never so. nevertheless, for all those cans of tuna A, B, C, D, and E keep us trotting to the supermarket where the clerks are all different also.
